L71: 
L72: 서울대학교 동물병원의 임상시험 모집 공고를 안내해 드립니다.
L73: 
L74: 【43†Image】
L75: 
L76:   * ### 【44†Image】목적
L77: 
L78: 서울대학교 수의과대학 동물병원에서는 ELEKTA사의 최첨단 선형가속기 및 방사선 치료 전용소프트웨어MONACO 6.0을 도입하여 방사선 치료 프로토콜 정립 및 임상 데이터 확보를 위한 임상 시험을 아래와 같이 실시하고자 합니다.
L79: 
L80:   * ### 【44†Image】지원 자격
L81: 
L82: 다음 사항에 해당하는 환자에게 지원 자격이 주어집니다.
L83: (1) 본원에서 종양을 진료받고 있는 환자
L84: (2) 조직검사를 실시하였거나 그에 준한 검사를 실시하여 종양의 종류가 확인된 환자
L85: (3) 방사선치료 일정을 따를 수 있는 환자 (내원 일정 및 총 횟수는 종양마다 다양)
L86: (4) 치료 후 추적관찰 일정에 따를 수 있는 환자: 치료 후 30일, 90일, 180일에 내원
L87: (5) 전신 상태가 비교적 양호하여 일반적인 방사선치료에 적합한 환자
L88: (6) 종양의 진행이 급진적이지 않은 환자
L89: (7) 마취에 대한 유의적인 위험성이 없는 환자
L90: (8) 치료 정보의 학술적 사용에 동의하는 환자
L91: 
L92: 다음의 경우 임상시험 지원에서 제외됩니다.
L93: 
L94: - 임상적으로 방사선치료가 지시되지 않는 환자 (예: 전신 종양)
L95: - 기타 수의사의 판단에 따라 연구 참여에 부적절하다고 판단되는 경우
L96: - 각 부위별 일정 수의 환자만을 모집하므로 이미 해당 부위 지원자가 많을 경우
L97: 
L98: ※ 본 임상시험은 서울대학교 동물병원 내원 환자에 한해 실시하며 방사선치료만을 위해 초진 내원하는 경우 제외됩니다.
L99:   * ### 【44†Image】임상 시험 참가 혜택
L100: 
L101: - 방사선치료 및 추적검사 비용의 10% 할인 (VAT 포함) 혜택
L102: 
L103: * 불포함 사항: 입원비, 방사선치료와 관련 없는 증상의 검사 및 치료비
L104: 
L105:   * ### 【44†Image】임상 시험 일정 및 유의사항
L106: 
L107: 본 임상시험은 23.06.14 부터 24.12.13 까지 진행되며, 두부 및 복부, 사지 등 부위별 제한된 환자 (O마리)를 모집하므로 각 부위별로 모집이 조기 마감될 수 있습니다.
L108: 
L109: 병원 내원 일정은 환자마다 다르며 일반적으로 상담1회, 시뮬레이션 CT촬영 1회, 방사선 치료 (3-20회), 추적검사 (0일, 30일, 90일, 180일 차)로 진행됩니다.
L110: 
L111: 방사선치료는 통원 혹은 입원치료로 진행 가능하며, 입원비는 환자가 부담합니다.
L112: 
L113: 방사선치료 후 180일째 진행되는 추적검사까지 참가하는 것이 전체과정이며, 환자의 임상적 상태와 무관히 임의중단할 경우 혜택받은 치료비에 대해 반환하셔야 합니다.
L114: 방사선치료는 종양 뿐 아니라 정상 세포의 손상을 유발하므로 치료 부위에 따라 다양한 후유증이 동반될 수 있으며, 이에 대한 치료는 환자가 부담합니다.
L115: 
L116:   * ### 【44†Image】임상 시험 참가 방법
L117: 
L118: (1) 서울대학교 동물병원의 담당 주치의에게 요청하면 방사선종양팀에 연결됩니다.
L119: (2) 방사선종양팀에서 진료 기록 확인 후 적합한 환자로 판단되면 상담 일정을 잡아드립니다.

L31: VCB-2401 VAXLEUKIN-15
L32: 
L33: Animal-Specific Immuno-Oncology Drugs: Market Insights
L34:   * Dogs suffer from cancer at rates higher than humans. The incidence of cancer in dogs is significantly elevated compared to humans—lymphoma occurs 2~5 times more often, mammary cancer 4 times, osteosarcoma 8 times, and skin cancer 35 times more frequently in dogs. For dogs aged 8 and older, the cancer incidence rate approaches 40~50%.
L35:   * Despite the growing market for pet medications, the development of new veterinary drugs has not kept pace with demand. Existing pet immuno-oncology drugs are primarily repurposed from human treatments, which often leads to lower efficacy and concerns about side effects when used in animals.
L36: 
L37:   * In response to this market demand, Vaxcellbio has developed VCB-2401(Vaxleukin-15), an immuno-oncology drug specifically for pets.
L38: 
L39: 【9†Image】 Pet Cancer Drug Market
L40: 
L41: 【10†Image】
L42: VCB-2401(Vaxleukin-15): Korea's first immunoadjuvant therapy exclusively for companion dogs
L43: 
L44:   * VCB-2401 is a recombinant drug developed based on canine interleukin-15, a cytokine secreted by canine white blood cells, using the Escherichia coli expression system.
L45:   * When administered to companion dogs, VCB-2401 activates immune cells such as NK cells and T cells, enhancing their anti-cancer immune functions. This immunotherapy not only shows strong anticancer efficacy but also ensures safety for pets, making it a reliable treatment option for dogs with cancer.
L46:   * In August 2024, the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency granted product approval for VCB-2401 as the first domestic immuno-oncology drug for companion animals (an adjuvant after mammary tumor surgery). In September 2025, the indications were expanded by granting product approval as an adjuvant treatment for canine lymphoma and mammary tumors.
L47: 
L48:   * Vaxcellbio plans to expand the indications for VCB-2401 to include feline diseases, following mammary tumors and lymphomas in dogs.
L49: 【9†Image】 VCB-2401(Vaxleukin-15)
L50: 
L51: 【11†Image】

L53: VCB-2401’s Mechanism of Action
L54: 
L55:   * When interleukin-15 binds to its receptor, it activates the JAK1 (Janus-associated kinase 1 protein through the beta chain (phosphorylation of tyrosine residues on JAK). This process induces the phosphorylation of STAT3/5 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 3/5) proteins via the gamma chain.
L56:   * During this process, immune cells within the body, such as NK cells and T cells, are activated, thereby enhancing anti-cancer effects.

L11: ## Pengenalan
L12: Veterinary and Comparative Oncology Department of Veterinary Clinical Studies Department of Veterinary Pathology and Microbiology FACULTY OF VETERINARY MEDICINE Synopsis: The main research areas are in the investigation of mechanisms of development, detection, monitoring, and treatment of animal cancers. The mechanisms of cancer development are investigated by determining pathways and molecules involved in cancer proliferation and regression.
L13: These pathways and molecules will serve as targets for intervention and induction therapies for cancers. In the early detection and monitoring of cancer development, several serum biomarkers have been identified, which have potential to be developed into diagnostic kits. The efficacies of new anticancer synthetic and natural compounds are aso investigated in dogs, cats, mice and rats with natural occurring and induced cancers.
L14: Some of these compounds will be packaged in new and innovative nanoparticle delivery systems for more effective therapies. The research also involves preclinical trials in the development of animal and human cancer therapeutics that would eventually culminate in commercialization. L24: 【10†For Pet Owners】【11†For Veterinarians and Scientists】
L25: ### What is Kv9?
L26: Kv9 is a treatment designed to help dogs with solid cancers by activating their own immune system to fight the disease. It is injected directly into the tumour, where it places a harmless “marker” on the cancer cells. This marker helps the immune system recognise the tumour, which is something it often struggles to do on its own.Once the immune system can recognise these cancer cells, it begins to attack them. In the process it can also learn how to attack them elsewhere in the body.
L27: Because the process works like a personalised vaccine, it should also help prevent the same type of cancer from returning.
L28: ### What animals are you accepting into the trial?
L29: 
L30: We are currently accepting dogs and cats into the clinical study. Horses can enrol if they are based in the Hawkes Bay region.
L31: 
L32: ### What cancers are eligible to participate in the trial?
L33: 
L34: We are currently enrolling dogs with soft tissue sarcomas, mast cell tumours, mammary gland tumours, melanoma, squamous cell carcinoma, anal sac tumours, and other accessible solid tumours.
L35: ### My dog had surgery on their tumour, can I still participate?
L36: 
L37: It depends. There needs to be at least 1cm x 1cm of tumour to receive the treatment. So if there is tissue remaining or if it has regrown after surgery they are still considered eligible for the trial.
L38: 
L39: ### Is Kv9 chemotherapy?
L40: 
L41: No, Kv9 is an immunotherapy. A significant benefit of immunotherapy is that it commonly is better tolerated and can provide a long lasting immune protection.
L42: ### What does the treatment involve?
L43: 
L44: If enrolled in the study, your pet will receive several small injections (less than 0.2mL at each site) of a Kv9 solution directly into their tumour mass every 14 days for up to three occasions. In some instances, a fourth dose may be considered after 3 months. In addition, there will be several follow-ups over the next two years to monitor their disease progression (there will be no charge for these follow-up appointments).
L45: ### Is Kv9 safe?
L46: 
L47: Kv9 is an experimental product and its safety cannot be guaranteed. In the current clinical study it has been well tolerated by the majority of participants. Most side effects are mild and temporary, such as tiredness, reduced appetite, or swelling at the tumour site.
L48: 
L49: ### Will this cure my pet?
L50: 
L51: Kv9 is an experimental treatment and cannot be guaranteed to cure cancer. The goal is to slow or stop tumour growth while maintaining good quality of life.
L52: ### Does it cost anything to participate in the trial?
L53: No, the Kv9 treatment is provided at no cost and necessary veterinary visits during the clinical study are covered by KVS. To be eligible for the clinical study your pet must have their tumour diagnosed by your primary care veterinarian, this is at your own cost. KVS will provide support if there are changes in your pet suspected to be caused by participating in the trial, this is often including financial support.
